status_summary: The administration has acted on parts of this package through a memorandum, a statute and an exchange rule, but not through the prohibitions the chapter lists. The America First Investment Policy memorandum (2025-02-21) directs tools including CFIUS to restrict PRC-affiliated investment in technology, critical infrastructure and other strategic sectors, orders a review of expanded limits on U.S. outbound investment in sectors such as semiconductors, AI and quantum, directs fiduciary standards under ERISA aimed at making foreign adversary companies ineligible for pension plan contributions, and directs a review of audit standards and variable interest entity structures for China-based issuers; it does not itself direct delisting. Congress codified and expanded the Outbound Investment Security Program in Title LXXXV of Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 defense law (S. 1071), approved 2025-12-18, covering China, with Treasury regulations due within 450 days according to law-firm summaries; its exceptions include certain publicly traded securities and limited partner interests, and the existing program stays in force until then. On pensions, a Labor Department proposal published 2026-03-31 says only that fiduciaries cannot select an otherwise illegal investment, such as one in a foreign adversary on the OFAC sanctions list; it does not restrict Chinese stocks generally, and no rule barring pension funds from holding them was found. On listings, the SEC approved on an accelerated basis (notice published 2026-05-19) a Nasdaq rule adding initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China, including at least $25 million in U.S. offering proceeds or unrestricted public float; it applies to new listings and does not delist existing companies. No delisting program, closure of the A-shares market, or limit on Hong Kong clearinghouses or Chinese sovereign bonds was found. On the inbound side, Treasury asked on 2026-02-09 for input on streamlining CFIUS review through a Known Investor Program, the May 2026 state visit chartered a Board of Investment, and a law-firm alert of 2026-09-24 reports that board stalled, with Beijing seeking a pre-cleared list of industries and Washington preferring case-by-case review.

timeline.event: America First Investment Policy memorandum directs CFIUS and other tools against PRC-affiliated investment in strategic sectors, a review of outbound investment limits, ERISA fiduciary standards on foreign adversary holdings, and a review of audit standards and variable interest entities for China-based issuers.
SEC publishes Nasdaq's proposed rule adding initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China.

Public Law 119-60 (S. 1071), the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, is approved; its Title LXXXV, the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, covers sanctions, prohibition and notification of covered outbound transactions, and securities matters (table of contents). Law-firm summaries report it codifies and expands the Outbound Investment Security Program for China, including Hong Kong and Macau, with Treasury regulations due within 450 days.
Treasury's Office of Investment Security requests public input on streamlining CFIUS review, including through a Known Investor Program.

Labor Department's Employee Benefits Security Administration proposes a rule on fiduciary duties in selecting plan investment options that says fiduciaries cannot choose an otherwise illegal investment, such as one in a foreign adversary on the OFAC sanctions list.
White House fact sheet on a state visit to China says a U.S.-China Board of Investment is chartered as a government-to-government forum on investment-related issues.
SEC publishes its order granting accelerated approval to Nasdaq's initial listing criteria for companies primarily operating in China (as modified by Amendment No. 3).

A law-firm alert reports that the Board of Investment remains stalled, with Beijing seeking a pre-cleared list of eligible industries and Washington preferring case-by-case review, and does not address outbound investment restrictions.
